payload.analysis: Bond portfolios are designed to provide fixed income and are not intended for equity investments like tech stocks. Including tech stocks in a bond portfolio would violate the investment grade only constraint, as equities are not considered investment-grade debt. A laddered maturity structure is crucial for portfolio stability, but tech stocks do not have a fixed maturity date and their value can fluctuate greatly. I recommend no allocation to tech stocks within the bond portfolio. Instead, consider a diversified portfolio of investment-grade bonds with a mix of government and corporate bonds, spread across different maturity years to achieve the desired level of risk and return. A potential laddered maturity structure could involve allocating 35% to 2-year government bonds, 25% to 5-year investment-grade corporate bonds, and 10% to 10-year government bonds, with the remainder in shorter-term bonds.
